title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.31869v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Covariate-aware time series foundation models (TSFMs) accept a future path for a control variable and return a forecast, inviting what-if queries. The query is interventional; the models are trained on observational data. We determine whether their answers are the conditional slope $\partial E[Y|X]$ or the interventional effect $\partial E[Y|do(X)]$, at three levels. Theory: a Bayes-optimal observational predictor answers interventional queries associationally unless the adjustment set is available and used; for in-context least squares we derive the resulting confounding gap -- a model's effect estimate under an observational minus under a randomized context -- in closed form, a parameter-free reference line. Behaviour: on a preregistered grid with exact counterfactual ground truth, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 all track this line ($R^2$ 0.90-1.00) and respond more confounded than regression itself (slopes 1.3-1.8), on

translated_title: 预测的是关联，而非干预：协变量感知时间序列基础模型的预注册因果审计
translated_abstract: 协变量感知的时间序列基础模型（TSFM）接受控制变量的未来路径并返回预测结果，这自然引发了“假如……会怎样”式的查询。然而这类查询本质上是干预性的，而这些模型却是在观测数据上训练的。我们在三个层面判定这些模型的回答究竟是条件斜率 ∂E[Y|X]（关联性）还是干预效应 ∂E[Y|do(X)]。理论层面：贝叶斯最优的观测性预测器只有在能够获取并使用调整集的情况下，才会以干预性方式回答干预查询，否则其回答仍是关联性的；针对上下文内最小二乘法，我们以闭式形式推导出由此产生的混淆差距——即模型在观测性情境与随机化情境下效应估计之差——这是一条无参数的参考线。行为层面：在一个预注册、且具有精确反事实真值的实验网格上，Chronos-2、TiRex-2、TabPFN-TS 和 TimesFM-2.5 全部贴合这条参考线（R² 为 0.90–1.00），并且比回归本身表现出更强的混淆响应（斜率为 1.3–1.8）……
tldr: 该研究通过理论与预注册实验证明，协变量感知的时间序列基础模型（如Chronos-2、TimesFM-2.5等）对“假如”式干预查询给出的只是关联性预测而非真实因果效应，并推导出闭式的无参数混淆差距参考线，实验显示这些模型比回归本身更严重地受混淆影响。
en_tdlr: This paper proves theoretically and confirms via preregistered experiments with exact counterfactual ground truth that covariate-aware time series foundation models (Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS, TimesFM-2.5) answer what-if queries associationally rather than interventionally, deriving a closed-form parameter-free confounding-gap reference line that these models track even more strongly than regression itself.
